subject_name: Wines, Beers, Spirits 1 (Nghiệp vụ pha chế đồ uống 1)

general_information.Description: A study of the beverage service of the Hospitality Industry including spirits, wines, beers and mixology beverages. Topics include purchasing, resource control, beverage storage and issuing, bar stocks and sales control, bar customer care, safety and security, managing bar wastage, the law and sale of liquor.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend more than 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Develop general knowledge on the origins and development of the beverage industry.
Identify local laws and customer in Vietnam pertaining to the service and purchase of alcoholic beverages and liquor law liability
Recognize equipment and glassware used for beverage preparation and service
Assemble the hand tools and equipment needed to mix and serve drinks and prepare garnishes.
Explain the procedures for internal beverage control
Explain the production processes for spirits, wine, beer, and other beverages
Identify and provide the process of preparation, presentation, and service of alcoholic beverages.
Identify and present the knowledge of wines by grape and other fruit variety, country, growing region, and production process.
Explain how to create a workforce of the beverage business operations.
Explain the purpose of effective beverage receiving and storage practices and how to calculate an inventory turnover rate.
Interpret financial data and use decision-making skills and abilities in a variety of managerial and service positions.

assessments.Note: Instruction and shedules for Progress tests must be presented in the Course Implementation Plan approved by director of the campus. Progress test must be taken right after the last lectures of required material. Instructor has resposibility to review the test for students after graded.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on topics of studied units
assessments.Note: All assignments should be typed and double-spaced with 11-point font, and must be submitted in soft copy. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission Evaluation will be based on both presentation and written report (reccommded 30%, 70% accordingly)

assessments.Question Type: Each student must be assessed through practical demonstration in a simulated workplace environment where beverage ingredients and equipment are provided. Competency is to be demonstrated by effectively preparing and serving beverage in accordance with the performance criteria and the range listed within the practical learning sessions.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on the practical learning sessions of the course.
assessments.Note: Practical assessment must ensure access to: fixtures and large equipment (bar service area, storage area for glassware and drinks…), small equipment (range of glassware, service trays and liners…), stock (liqueurs, wines, basic spirits, wide commercial range of non-alcoholic beverages)

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice, exercises or essay questions
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Quizzes will test for knowledge of subjects in the chapter assigned for that day.
assessments.Note: These quizzes will be given at various times during class (beginning, middle or end). Total number of quizzes: 2

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: The questions/ exercises will cover the lectures, class discussions, activities, exercises, and textbook.
